def test_correct_bracketing():
    # Simple valid cases
    assert correct_bracketing("<") is False          # unclosed
    assert correct_bracketing("<>") is True           # basic pair
    assert correct_bracketing("<<><>>") is True       # nested
    assert correct_bracketing("><") is False          # closes before opening

    # Empty string: balanced (depth 0)
    assert correct_bracketing("") is True

    # Multiple sequential pairs
    assert correct_bracketing("<><><>") is True

    # Deeply nested
    assert correct_bracketing("<<<>>>") is True

    # Extra closers at end
    assert correct_bracketing("<>>") is False

    # Extra opener at start, never recovers
    assert correct_bracketing("<<>") is False

    # Negative depth mid-string, recovers, but must fail
    assert correct_bracketing("><<>") is False

    # Long balanced string
    assert correct_bracketing("<" * 1000 + ">" * 1000) is True

    # Long unbalanced string
    assert correct_bracketing("<" * 1000 + ">" * 999) is False
